title: Velocity–time graphs
keyIdea: On a velocity–time graph, the gradient is the acceleration and the area underneath is the displacement.

kid: A velocity–time graph shows how fast something moves at each moment. Time goes across and velocity goes up.
A flat line means a steady speed. A line going up means speeding up. The steepness tells you the acceleration. The area under the line tells you how far it went.
adult: Gradient = change in velocity ÷ time taken = acceleration, in m/s². A negative gradient is a deceleration.
Area under the graph = displacement. Split it into rectangles and triangles: a car accelerating from rest to 10 m/s in 4 s travels ½ × 4 × 10 = 20 m.

familyTip: On a car journey, note the speed every 10 seconds. Sketch the graph and find where the car sped up, slowed down and cruised.

practice.prompt: A flat line on a velocity–time graph means…
practice.explain: Constant velocity: steady speed, not necessarily stopped.

practice.prompt: Velocity rises from 0 to {v} m/s in {t} s. What is the acceleration in m/s²?
A runner moves at a steady {v} m/s for {t} s. What area is under the graph, in metres?
What does the area under a velocity–time graph give?
practice.explain: Velocity × time is distance moved, so the area gives displacement.

pool.prompt: A car accelerates steadily from rest to {v} m/s in {t} s. How far does it go, in metres?
pool.hint: Area of a triangle: ½ × base × height.

pool.prompt: A line sloping down towards the time axis shows…
choices: going backwards at a steady speed

pool.prompt: A bus slows from {u} m/s to 0 in {t} s. What is the size of the deceleration, in m/s²?

pool.explain: A straight line has a constant gradient.

pool.prompt: Speed {v} m/s for {a} s, then {v} m/s for {b} more seconds. What is the total distance, in metres?
What are the units of acceleration?
Two cars: A's line is steeper than B's. Which has the greater acceleration?
pool.explain: A greater gradient means a greater acceleration.

visual.caption: Velocity v = 2t (speeding up from rest). Drag the end time: the shaded area is the distance travelled.
